title: Purification and preparation of Rhodobacter sphaeroides reaction centers for photocurrent measurements and atomic force microscopy characterization
protocol: Inoculate 10 mL LB supplemented with 25 μg/mL kanamycin in a test tube with R. sphaeroides cells containing the pIND4-DM plasmid from a glycerol freezer stock.
Grow overnight culture for approximately 24 hours at 30°C, shaken or rotated on a wheel.
Add 10 mL of the overnight culture to a 1 L Erlenmeyer flask containing 200 mL LB supplemented with 25 μg/mL kanamycin.
Grow in 1L Erlenmeyer flask for approximately 24 hours at 30°C, shaken at 200 RPM.
Split the 200 mL overnight culture into four 50 mL aliquots.
Add each 50 mL aliquot to one of four 2 L Erlenmeyer flasks containing 500 mL RLB supplemented with kanamycin at a final concentration of 25 μg/mL.
Add isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) to each flask to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM for protein induction.
Grow the cultures for 16 hours at 30°C, shaken at 200 RPM.
Pellet cells by centrifuging at 12000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C in a J-LITE JLA 8.1000 rotor or equivalent.
Discard the supernatant and weigh the cell pellet (wet mass).
Resuspend the cell pellet using resuspension buffer, with 2 mL of buffer per gram of cell pellet.
Stir to thoroughly mix if the pellet is frozen.
Lysate cells by passing through a French pressure cell press chilled to 4°C at a pressure between 22500 and 25000 PSI.
Ensure that the lysate is not very viscous.
Add more DNase to the lysate if it is too viscous and stir gently for 1-2 min until no longer viscous.
Centrifuge the lysate at 10,000×g for 20 min at 4°C in a JA-20 rotor or equivalent.
Pipette the supernatant into a separate beaker.
Stir the supernatant in the dark at room temperature (19°C–21°C).
Add 30% N,N-dimethyldodecylamine N-oxide solution dropwise to achieve a final concentration of 1%.
Add 2 M imidazole to a final concentration of 5 mM and stir for 20-30 min.
Centrifuge the solubilized solution at 164,000×g for 20 min at 4°C in a Type 70 Ti rotor or equivalent.
Pipette the supernatant into a new beaker.
Dilute the supernatant tenfold with wash buffer.
Measure the absorbance spectrum (250 nm–1000 nm) of the diluted supernatant.
Centrifuge the sample again at 164000×g for 20 minutes at 4°C if turbidity is observed.
Equilibrate clean Ni2+-NTA agarose resin with 2 column volumes wash buffer.
Transfer the equilibrated resin into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add the supernatant to the 50 mL conical tube containing the resin.
Rock gently overnight (15–18 hours) in the dark at 4°C.
Pour the overnight resin suspension onto a gravity column.
Allow liquid to flow through into a clean beaker.
Measure the absorbance spectrum of the flowthrough, diluted 10-fold in wash buffer.
Compare this spectrum of the flowthrough to the spectrum of the starting material supernatant.
Add wash buffer continuously to the column.
Measure the absorbance spectrum of the flowthrough, undiluted, after approximately 5 column volumes of wash buffer.
Monitor the absorbance at 280 nm every 50–100 mL of wash buffer.
Wash until the absorbance value plateaus to <0.05 AU.
Allow the wash buffer to drain to the surface of the resin.
Add 5 column volumes of elution buffer to the column.
Allow the buffer to flow slowly.
Monitor the colour of the eluent.
Start collecting the sample once a pale purple colour is visible (i.e., A804 >0.015 AU).
Collect until the flowthrough is no longer coloured.
Measure the absorbance spectrum of the elution, diluted 20- or 50-fold in elution buffer.
Dilute RCs 10-fold in wash buffer if storing overnight.
Buffer exchange the RCs into PBS pH 7.2 and 0.03% LDAO using a 15 mL 100 kDa NMWL centrifugal filter unit.
Add the eluent to a 100 kDa NMWL centrifugal filter unit.
Centrifuge at 5000×g for 25 min until the volume of the retentate is less than 0.5 mL, then discard the flowthrough.
Add PBS to the retentate to a final volume of 15 mL.
Centrifuge at 5000×g for 25 min at 4°C in a JS-5.3 rotor or equivalent.
Discard the flowthrough and repeat the previous step until the volume of the retentate is less than 0.5 mL.
Buffer exchange the RCs into the anion loading buffer using a 15 mL 100 kDa NMWL centrifugal filter unit.
Add the eluent to the 100 kDa NMWL centrifugal filter unit.
Centrifuge at 5000×g for 25 min at 4°C in a JS-5.3 rotor or equivalent.
Discard the flowthrough and repeat the previous step until the volume of the retentate is less than 0.5 mL.
Add anion loading buffer to the retentate to a final volume of 15 mL.
Centrifuge at 5000×g for 25 min at 4°C in a JS-5.3 rotor or equivalent.
Discard the flowthrough and repeat the previous step until the volume of the retentate is less than 0.5 mL.
Equilibrate the anion exchange resin with approximately 5 column volumes of anion loading buffer.
Allow the buffer to drain to the surface of the resin.
Gently add the RCs to the column, ensuring the resin bed is not disturbed.
Let the sample flow through.
Add 5 column volumes of anion loading buffer and collect the flowthrough in approximately 5 mL aliquots.
Measure the absorbance spectrum of each flowthrough aliquot.
Monitor the absorbance at 804 nm to determine if RCs are bound or eluting.
RCs can be considered to be eluting if A804 is over 0.015 AU.
Add more buffer until the RCs have stopped eluting.
Repeat the previous step at increasing concentrations of NaCl: 5 mM, 10 mM, 30 mM, 60 mM, and 80 mM.
Pool the fractions of RCs with sufficient purity (i.e., A280:A804 ratio of <1.4).
Proceed to step 17 to buffer exchange the RCs into PBS pH 7.2.
Rinse a glass electrochemical cell with ddH2O followed by 100 mM KOH.
Fill the cell with 100 mM KOH such that the gold electrode is fully immersed.
Clean gold flag electrodes electrochemically by cyclic voltammetry using a potentiostat.
Gently bubble the electrolyte with argon gas to remove dissolved oxygen.
Connect the gold electrode to the working electrode lead from the potentiostat.
Connect a flamed annealed platinum electrode to the counter electrode lead.
Connect an Ag/AgCl reference electrode rinsed in ddH2O to the reference electrode lead.
Ensure that all electrodes are fully submerged in the electrolyte.
Set up a CV with the following parameters: Scan rate 25 mV/s, lower vertex −1.25 V vs. Ag/AgCl, upper vertex +0.55 V vs. Ag/AgCl, cycles 15.
Rinse the gold electrode with ddH2O after cleaning is complete.
Hold the gold stem using tweezers and flame anneal the gold electrode until it turns dark orange in colour.
Store the cleaned electrode in a clean and sealed container, ensuring the surface does not touch the sides.
Fully submerge a cleaned gold electrode in 100 μL of an RC solution in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube of the desired concentration (e.g., 0.5–10 μM).
Incubate for the desired period of time (e.g., 10 min to 24 h) in the dark at 4°C.
Rinse the electrode to remove excess RCs by gently dipping in PBS.
Fully submerge an RC-deposited gold electrode in 100 μL of a 100 μM MCH solution in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate for the desired period of time (e.g., 1–24 h) in the dark at 4°C.
Rinse the electrode by gently dipping in PBS.
The electrode should be used immediately.
Set up an electrochemical cell with 2 mL of PBS in a cuvette.
Insert the gold working electrode into the cuvette.
Insert the platinum counter electrode into the cuvette.
Insert the Ag/AgCl reference electrode into the cuvette.
Connect the electrodes to a potentiostat.
Add an aliquot of 1 M hydroquinone in DMSO to achieve the desired final concentration (e.g., 1–20 mM).
Run a CV with a scan rate of 2 mV/s.
Set the upper voltage to 0.30 V vs. Ag/AgCl.
Set the lower voltage to −0.10 V vs. Ag/AgCl.
Perform 2 scans.
Ensure that the measured currents are small (i.e., <10 μA/cm²).
Apply a 13 Hz sine wave to the LEDs to illuminate the gold flag electrode.
Ensure the sine wave amplitude does not exceed the offset current.
Set the LED driver with a 40 mA offset and add a peak-to-peak current of 70 mA.
Adjust amplification settings on the lock-in amplifier to increase signal levels.
Set the lock-in amplifier filters at 24 dB roll-off and time constant of 1 or 3 s.
Measure the amplitude output from the lock-in amplifier simultaneously with total current.
Adjust the conversion on the potentiostat to ensure the input to the lock-in amplifier is not too large.
Determine the photocurrent magnitude using the potentiostat and lock-in amplifier settings.
Begin photocurrent measurements at 0 V vs. Ag/AgCl.
Obtain a stable photocurrent signal (approximately 15 s at 0 V vs. Ag/AgCl).
Scan the potential slowly to +0.3 V vs. Ag/AgCl and then to -0.1 V vs. Ag/AgCl repeatedly at 2 mV/s.
Record the potential, total current, and amplitude from the lock-in amplifier every 0.1 s.
Measure DC photocurrents at the open circuit potential (OCP) of the electrochemical cell.
Monitor the potential in the dark (LEDs off) until stabilized (approximately 2 min).
Cut approximately 1.5 cm of gold wire (1 mm in diameter) and secure to a holder using additional gold wire and glass tubing.
Rinse the gold wire with ddH2O thoroughly.
Immerse the wire in a solution of aqua regia (1:3 ratio (v/v) of HNO3:HCl) for 10 min.
Rinse with ddH2O again.
Flame the gold wire until the tip of the wire melts.
Stop melting when the bead climbs slightly up the wire.
Rinse the gold wire with ddH2O thoroughly.
Immerse the wire in a solution of aqua regia for 10 min.
Rinse with ddH2O again.
Repeat the previous two steps until the bead reaches approximately 2–3 mm in diameter.
Examine the etching pattern under a microscope to look for a highly symmetrical pattern corresponding to the crystallography.
Melt the electrode to smooth out the surface once the bead has a symmetric etch pattern and no grain boundaries are visible.
Check for the presence of a large flat reflective region on the surface, which is the 111 facet.
Repeat melting and cooling until the 111 facet region is approximately 0.1 mm in diameter to place the AFM tip on it.
Do not let the molten gold go past the top of the bead when remelting; withdraw the flame before it reaches the stem.
Stop melting immediately if the flame reaches the stem to retain the single crystal pattern.
Ensure that the electrode retains its single crystal character after each remelting process.
Assemble a glass electrochemical cell for cleaning the electrode surface using a 0.1 M NaOH solution and purge with argon.
Connect the single crystal gold electrode to the working electrode lead from the potentiostat.
Connect a flamed annealed platinum electrode to the counter electrode lead.
Connect a rinsed saturated calomel reference electrode to the reference electrode lead.
Set up a CV with the following parameters: Scan rate 50 mV/s, Lower vertex −1.4 V vs. SCE, Upper vertex +0.6 V vs. SCE, Cycles 30.
Rinse the gold electrode with ddH2O and flame anneal carefully to avoid overheating.
Store the cleaned single crystal gold bead electrode in a clean, sealed container such that the surface is not in contact with the sides.
Rinse the single crystal gold bead electrode with PBS for 10 seconds.
Rinse the electrode with ddH2O for 30 seconds to remove residual salt.
Dry the electrode under a stream of argon.
Mount the electrode on the AFM stage.
Transfer the electrode to an optical microscope to coarsely align the 111 facet horizontally.
Illuminate the electrode surface in the AFM holder with the output from a columnated laser diode.
By moving the bead using tweezers, align the reflected beam with the path of the incident light.
Transfer the finely aligned electrode on the AFM sample holder to the AFM microscope.
Find the 111 facet as a bright oval spot when illuminated with white light in the AFM.
Approach the tip to the surface as usual.
Perform a force curve measurement using tapping mode to ensure good contact with the surface and to determine the surface quality.
Scan at a frequency of 0.14 lines/sec, sampling 4096 lines per image.
Repeat scanning as necessary.
Process raw AFM images.
Process AFM images using Gwyddion.
Correct the background of the AFM images.
Correct the tilt of the AFM images.
Remove planar background or tilt from the AFM image using the “Remove Polynomial Background” method.
Fit a polynomial to the whole image in both X and Y dimensions for background correction.
Choose a polynomial order no higher than 3rd order.
Use 1st order correction to remove the tilt from the image.
Apply the “Align Rows” option to correct low frequency waves present after 1st order correction.
Monitor RMS roughness using the “Statistical Quantities” method during flattening process.
Limit background correction to where it no longer affects the RMS roughness values.
Perform a particle analysis (size, height) after obtaining a flattened image.
Set a threshold of 1 nm and create a mask.
Erode the mask twice.
Dilate the mask once.
Watershed the resulting image to delineate or separate the particles.
Create a histogram of the maximum height for each particle.
Create a histogram of the distribution of the footprint area for each particle.
